open_questions: Centroid inconclusive because no sector with a clear difference image (centroid.verdict inconclusive) leaves the signal on-target unconfirmed, but the on-target binary evidence does not require a neighbour.
dossier.public_summary: The dips alternate between shallow and very deep, and two transits even vanish, which does not match a planet on one star. Early sectors show a deep signal while a later sector shows almost no signal. Together this is an eclipsing binary on the target seen at half its true 18.9-day period, not a planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ at 6.05 sigma, with deeper even dips, indicating period is half the true binary period (9.46 d vs 18.9 d). This is the classic on-target eclipsing binary signature at twice the search period.

Depths are wildly inconsistent; two early transits are ~3x mean depth and the two recent transits are consistent with zero. A planet on this star must be consistent across all transits; dominance by a few outliers is false-positive evidence.
